Question:
Can we still use the 50-hour allowance in AD 2013-11-11 when a switch reaches 3,000 hours?

Source: PROC-R7, section 3
3.1 Tracking. Time-controlled parts are listed in the fleet register, sheet Time-controlled parts, with the airframe hours at installation. The hours used on a part are the airframe's current total time minus the airframe hours at installation.
3.2 Engine oil pressure switch. AD 2013-11-11 limits the engine oil pressure switch, P/N 83278, to 3,000 hours time-in-service on the airplanes within its applicability. Anfa applies the same 3,000-hour limit to every Cessna 172R and 172S it maintains, including those outside the directive's serial number ranges. Plan the replacement when a switch reaches 2,900 hours. Keep two switches in stock.
3.3 When the records disagree. If the fleet register and a work order or logbook give different hours for the same installation, use the lower airframe hours at installation until the quality manager has resolved the difference. Never use the figure that gives the part more time.

Source: AD-2013-11-11, section (g)
If after the inspection required in paragraph (g)(1) of this AD it is confirmed that P/N 83278 engine oil pressure switch is installed, through inspection of the airplane or engine logbooks determine the TIS of the engine oil pressure switch.
If after the inspection required in paragraph (g)(1) of this AD you cannot positively identify the hours TIS on the P/N 83278 engine oil pressure switch, before further flight, replace the engine oil pressure switch with a new, zero time, P/N 83278 engine oil pressure switch. Record the engine oil pressure switch part number, date, and airplane hours in the airplane log book. The recorded engine oil pressure switch TIS will be used as the benchmark for calculation of the 3,000 hour TIS limit on the engine oil pressure switch.
(6) When the engine oil pressure switch is at or greater than 3,000 hours TIS or within 50 hours TIS after August 1, 2013 (the effective date of this AD), whichever occurs later, and repetitively thereafter at intervals not to exceed 3,000 hours TIS on the P/N

Source: AD-2013-11-11, section Authority
04-01 applies to the specified products. The SNPRM published in the Federal Register on March 7, 2013 (78 FR 14726). The NPRM (77 FR 60062, October 2, 2012) proposed to increase the applicability of the AD and place a life-limit of 3,000 hours time-in-service (TIS) on the engine oil pressure switch, requiring replacement when the engine oil pressure switch reaches its life limit. The SNPRM proposed to change the applicable serial numbers ranges and place a life-limit of 3,000 hours TIS on the engine oil pressure switch, requiring replacement when the engine oil pressure switch reaches its life limit.

Source: AD-2013-11-11, section (g)
At the next scheduled oil change, annual inspection, or 100-hour time-inservice (TIS) inspection after August 1, 2013 (the effective date of this AD), whichever occurs later, but in no case later than 12 months after August 1, 2013 (the effective date of this AD), inspect the engine oil pressure switch to determine if it is partnumber (P/N) 77041 or P/N 83278.
If after the inspection required in paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, P/N 77041 engine oil pressure switch is installed, before further flight, replace the engine oil pressure switch with a new, zero time, P/N 83278 engine oil pressure switch. Record the engine oil pressure switch part number, date, and airplane hours TIS in the airplane log book. The recorded engine oil pressure switch TIS will be used as the benchmark for calculation of the 3,000 hour TIS limit on the engine oil pressure switch.
After August 1, 2013 (the effective date of this AD), do not install a P/N 77041 engine oil pressure switch on any affected airplane.

Source: AD-2013-11-11, section Airworthiness
AGENCY: Federal Aviation
Administration (FAA), DOT.
ACTION: Final rule.
SUMMARY: We are superseding AD 200004-01 that applies to certain Cessna Aircraft Company (Cessna) Models 172R, 172S, 182S, 182T, T182T, 206H, and T206H airplanes. AD 2000-04-01 currently requires an inspection of the engine oil pressure switch and, if applicable, replacement of the engine oil pressure switch. This AD increases the applicability of the AD, places a lifelimit of 3,000 hours time-in-service on the engine oil pressure switch, and requires replacement when the engine oil pressure switch reaches its life limit. This AD was prompted by new reports of internal failure of the engine oil pressure switch, which could result in complete loss of engine oil with consequent partial or complete loss of engine power or fire. We are issuing this AD to correct the unsafe condition on these products.
DATES: This AD is effective August 1, 2013.
The Director of the Federal Register approved the incorporation by reference of certain publications listed in the AD as of August 1, 2013.

message.content:
Based on the supplied passages, the 50-hour allowance in AD 2013-11-11 is **not** a general allowance for when a switch reaches 3,000 hours. It was a one-time transition provision tied to the AD's effective date.

**Source: AD-2013-11-11, section (g)**
> "When the engine oil pressure switch is at or greater than 3,000 hours TIS **or within 50 hours TIS after August 1, 2013 (the effective date of this AD), whichever occurs later**, and repetitively thereafter at intervals not to exceed 3,000 hours TIS on the P/N..."

The text establishes two distinct triggers for the initial replacement action:
1.  The switch reaching **3,000 hours TIS**.
2.  The switch being **within 50 hours TIS after August 1, 2013** (the effective date).

The phrase "whichever occurs later" means the 50-hour window only applies to switches that were already near the limit when the AD became effective in 2013. For all subsequent replacements, the requirement is simply "at intervals not to exceed 3,000 hours TIS."

**Source: PROC-R7, section 3.2** reinforces the hard 3,000-hour limit without mentioning a 50-hour operational allowance: "Plan the replacement when a switch reaches 2,900 hours."

From AD-2013-11-11, section (g): "When the engine oil pressure switch is at or greater than 3,000 hours TIS or within 50 hours TIS after August 1, 2013 (the effective date of this AD), whichever occurs later, and repetitively thereafter at intervals not to exceed 3,000 hours TIS on the P/N"

This passage seems to be cut off, but it mentions "within 50 hours TIS after August 1, 2013 (the effective date of this AD), whichever occurs later". This suggests there's a 50-hour allowance related to the effective date of the AD, not related to reaching 3,000 hours.

The question asks: "Can we still use the 50-hour allowance in AD 2013-11-11 when a switch reaches 3,000 hours?"

From the text: "When the engine oil pressure switch is at or greater than 3,000 hours TIS or within 50 hours TIS after August 1, 2013 (the effective date of this AD), whichever occurs later..."

This phrasing suggests the 50-hour allowance is specifically about the period after the effective date (August 1, 2013), not about when a switch reaches 3,000 hours. The "whichever occurs later" compares "at or greater than 3,000 hours TIS" with "within 50 hours TIS after August 1, 2013". So the 50-hour allowance is a one-time transition provision for switches that were already close to 3,000 hours when the AD became effective.

The PROC-R7 document says "Plan the replacement when a switch reaches 2,900 hours." This suggests a 100-hour planning buffer, not a 50-hour allowance for operation past 3,000 hours.

Based on the provided passages, the 50-hour allowance appears to be a transition provision for the AD's effective date, not an ongoing allowance when a switch reaches 3,000 hours. The AD requires replacement when the switch reaches 3,000 hours TIS (or at the next inspection if within 50 hours after August 1, 2013, whichever is later).

So the answer appears to be no, the 50-hour allowance is not for when a switch reaches 3,000 hours in general; it was a one-time transition provision related to the AD's effective date.
